page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.16-256 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, the compute resources derive from 16 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.25 GHz with two threads per core. The memory-to-vCPU allocation equates to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing this shape in a high-density memory profile relative to typical compute configurations.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe or solid-state storage, requiring users to rely on network-attached block storage for persistence and high-volume input/output workloads. Furthermore, the configuration lacks dedicated GPU accelerators, confining its compute scope entirely to the host AMD EPYC processor. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned alongside the instance for external connectivity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the flexible allocation model allows organizations to acquire substantial memory density alongside dedicated compute resources without paying for unneeded GPU hardware. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive environments, in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, analytics processing, and enterprise application servers requiring large working sets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.16-256 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. The underlying hardware is powered by an AMD EPYC 7742 processor operating at 2.25 GHz across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. With an 8.0 GB memory-per-vCPU allocation, this shape offers a high-density RAM footprint designed for memory-constrained workloads. It does not include integrated local disk storage, depending on remote block storage solutions for persistent data, and features no hardware GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource profile provides a balance of dedicated CPU capacity and expansive memory, suiting it for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data processing pipelines, and enterprise application backends.
